source_en: J1, Cross-border birth and initial vaccination. In Country A (XXR, the birth country) the provincial hospital gives a newborn who is not its own country's national the Hep B and BCG birth doses and issues one signed DVC per dose (DVCMinPreQual at subclaim -6) as a paper QR, with no national identity number needed (the WHO guide's QR Code Generation section 12 example is such a pair). The hospital system is the Issuer (SMART Trust) and the HCERT side of the VHL Sharer; the private key stays with the key holder (two-phase signing, STT-ISS-004, STT-COS-006). XXR's DSC, under its CSCA, being on the GDHCN trust list is a PRECONDITION of issuing, declared below, not a step. The caregiver is the Holder (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) and VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL).
back_translation_en: J1, Cross-border birth and initial vaccination. In Country A (XXR, the country of birth), the provincial hospital administers to a newborn who is not a national of that country the hepatitis B and BCG birth doses and issues one signed DVC per dose (DVCMinPreQual at sub-claim -6) as a paper QR code, without any national identity number being needed (the example in section 12 QR Code Generation of the WHO guide is such a pair). The hospital's system is the issuer (SMART Trust) and the HCERT side of the VHL Sharer; the private key stays with the key holder (two-phase signing, STT-ISS-004, STT-COS-006). The presence of XXR's DSC, issued under its CSCA, on the GDHCN trust list is a PRECONDITION of issuance, declared below, and not a step. The caregiver is the holder (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) and the VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL).

Back in Country B (home, XXH), where the family resides, the community health worker finds an infant born abroad who is missing from the household roster on a home visit. source_en: J3, Clinic verification and schedule generation, in Country B. The clinic EHR (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, VHL Receiver side in IHE ITI VHL) holds a copy of the GDHCN trust list, which the trust anchor (Trust Network Anchor; IHE Trust Anchor) distributes and Country B, a Trust Network Participant, retrieves (smart-trust-phw retrieve-pki-material). Loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the clinic may be offline throughout, so the list it verifies against is the one it last refreshed, about weekly, when the CHW visits the base clinic or district health office. It verifies each foreign DVC in the STT-VER-001 order against XXR's DSC DID document, imports the verified doses with provenance, adds the national schedule code beside each foreign vaccine code (ConceptMap; the nurse decides any product with no mapping) and evaluates the national schedule, which finds the 6-week doses due and books them.

Loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, and not one of its steps: the clinic may be offline during the whole visit; the list against which it verifies is therefore the one it last refreshed, about once a week, when the CHW goes to the referral clinic or the district health office. source_en: J4.0, Outbound family travel, "One Family, One Phone". The shared phone holds the QRs for the caregiver, the VHL Holder. The records themselves stay hosted in Country B: the QR carries only a pointer and a key.

source_en: J4.1. Abroad, a child of the family needs care. The caregiver, the VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL; Holder in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver), opens her QR on the family phone and tells the passcode. The hospital system, a VHL Receiver (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw), verifies the HCERT against the GDHCN trust list, requests the manifest by ITI-YY5 with an HTTP Message Signature (STT-VHL-005, STT-VHL-006, STT-VHL-008) and decrypts the documents (STT-VHL-007). Country B's portal checks the passcode, returns the manifest and logs every request, granted or refused, as an AuditEvent at home (IHE BALP). If the HCERT does not verify, there is no digital verification: the VHL is not followed and the records are treated like paper. As in J3, loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the hospital verifies against its cached copy of the trust list and needs no connection to do so. It refreshes that cache nightly or hourly, where an offline site such as the J3 clinic refreshes about weekly.

The caregiver, VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL; holder in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver), opens her QR code on the family phone and gives the passcode. The hospital's system, VHL Receiver (receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw), verifies the HCERT against the GDHCN trust list, requests the manifest via ITI-YY5 with an HTTP Message Signature (STT-VHL-005, STT-VHL-006, STT-VHL-008) and decrypts the documents (STT-VHL-007). Country B's portal checks the passcode, returns the manifest and logs each request, granted or refused, as an AuditEvent in the country of origin (IHE BALP). If the HCERT is not verified, there is no digital verification: the VHL is not followed and the records are treated as paper documents. As in J3, loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, and not one of its steps: the hospital verifies against its cached copy of the trust list and needs no connection to do so. It refreshes this cache nightly or hourly, whereas an offline site like the J3 clinic refreshes it about once a week.

source_en: Thailand and Lao PDR never connect to each other. Both build on WHO GDHCN. Thailand publishes the key it signs certificates with, and Lao PDR caches the trust list, so its clinics can verify a Thai card with no signal. source_en: J1, Cross-border birth and initial vaccination. In Country A (XXR, the birth country) the provincial hospital gives a newborn who is not its own country's national the Hep B and BCG birth doses and issues one signed DVC per dose (DVCMinPreQual at subclaim -6) as a paper QR, with no national identity number needed (the WHO guide's QR Code Generation section 12 example is such a pair). The hospital system is the Issuer (SMART Trust) and the HCERT side of the VHL Sharer; the private key stays with the key holder (two-phase signing, <a0>STT-ISS-004</a0>, <a1>STT-COS-006</a1>). XXR's DSC, under its CSCA, being on the GDHCN trust list is a PRECONDITION of issuing, declared below, not a step. The caregiver is the Holder (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) and VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL).
back_translation_en: J1, Cross-border birth and initial vaccination. In Country A (XXR, the country of birth), the provincial hospital administers to a newborn who is not a national of that country the hepatitis B and BCG birth doses and issues one signed DVC per dose (DVCMinPreQual at sub-claim -6) as a paper QR, with no national identity number needed (the example in section 12 "QR Code Generation" of the WHO guide is such a pair). The hospital's system is the issuer (SMART Trust) and the HCERT side of the VHL sharer; the private key stays with the key holder (two-phase signing, <a0>STT-ISS-004</a0>, <a1>STT-COS-006</a1>). The presence of XXR's DSC, placed under its CSCA, on the GDHCN trust list is a PRECONDITION of issuance, declared below, not a step. The caregiver is the holder (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) and the VHL holder (IHE ITI VHL).

source_en: J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant in Country B
back_translation_en: J2 Find and refer an unregistered infant in Country B

source_en: J2, Return home, CHW discovery and referral. Back in Country B (home, XXH), where the family resides, the community health worker finds an infant born abroad who is missing from the household roster on a home visit. Offline, the CHW app adds the infant to the household (a FHIR Group, through a structured data capture form), reads the foreign DVCs without verifying them (read-unverified, <a0>STT-VER-011</a0>: the triage read stops before the trust lookup and marks every field unverified), saves the doses as reported by the family, not verified (Immunization.primarySource false), and refers the infant to the clinic for verification. Everything is queued on the phone and syncs when it next has a signal. The CHW app is a Receiver (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) that deliberately stops before trust; the caregiver provides the VDHC as Holder (smart-trust-phw requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver).
back_translation_en: J2, Return home, discovery and referral by the community health worker. Back in Country B (home, XXH), where the family lives, the community health worker discovers, during a home visit, a foreign-born infant who is not in the household register. Offline, the CHW application adds the infant to the household (a FHIR Group, by means of a structured data capture form), reads the foreign DVCs without verifying them (unverified read, <a0>STT-VER-011</a0>: the triage read stops before the trust lookup and marks every field as unverified), records the doses as declared by the family, unverified (Immunization.primarySource false), and refers the infant to the health centre for verification. Everything is queued on the phone and synchronized as soon as it has signal again. The CHW application is a receiver (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) that deliberately stops short of trust; the caregiver provides the VDHC as holder (smart-trust-phw requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver).

source_en: J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home clinic
back_translation_en: J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home health centre

source_en: J3, Clinic verification and schedule generation, in Country B. The clinic EHR (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, VHL Receiver side in IHE ITI VHL) holds a copy of the GDHCN trust list, which the trust anchor (Trust Network Anchor; IHE Trust Anchor) distributes and Country B, a Trust Network Participant, retrieves (smart-trust-phw retrieve-pki-material). Loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the clinic may be offline throughout, so the list it verifies against is the one it last refreshed, about weekly, when the CHW visits the base clinic or district health office. It verifies each foreign DVC in the <a0>STT-VER-001</a0> order against XXR's DSC DID document, imports the verified doses with provenance, adds the national schedule code beside each foreign vaccine code (ConceptMap; the nurse decides any product with no mapping) and evaluates the national schedule, which finds the 6-week doses due and books them.
back_translation_en: J3, Health centre verification and schedule generation, in Country B. The health centre's EHR (receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, VHL receiver side in IHE ITI VHL) holds a copy of the GDHCN trust list, which the trust anchor (trust network anchor; IHE trust anchor) distributes and which Country B, a participant in the trust network, retrieves (smart-trust-phw retrieve-pki-material). Loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step of it: the health centre may be offline for the whole visit; the list it verifies against is therefore the one it last refreshed, about once a week, when the community health worker goes to the referral health centre or the district health office. It verifies each foreign DVC in the order of <a0>STT-VER-001</a0> against the DID document of XXR's DSC, imports the verified doses with their provenance, adds the national schedule code next to each foreign vaccine code (ConceptMap; the nurse decides on any product without a match) and evaluates the national schedule, which determines that the 6-week doses are due and schedules them.
verdict: warn: "the base clinic" became "the referral health centre" (D233 keeps "base clinic")

source_en: J4.0 Issue the family's records to one phone as VHLs
back_translation_en: J4.0 Issue the family's records on a single phone as VHLs

source_en: J4.0, Outbound family travel, "One Family, One Phone". Before travelling, the caregiver who holds the family's one shared phone asks Country B's national portal for each family member's records, choosing for each a passcode the family can say aloud and an expiry (for example 14 days); the portal records that choice as the holder's consent to share (FHIR Consent, IHE Privacy Consent on FHIR). The portal, a VHL Sharer (IHE ITI VHL) and Issuer (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw), issues one passcode-protected Verifiable Health Link per member: the documents (IPS, DVCs) encrypted as JWE (<a0>STT-VHL-007</a0>) behind an ITI-YY5 manifest, the link in the SMART Health Links payload format at HCERT key 5 (<a1>STT-VHL-001</a1>, <a2>STT-VHL-002</a2>), signed with Country B's DSC. The shared phone holds the QRs for the caregiver, the VHL Holder. The records themselves stay hosted in Country B: the QR carries only a pointer and a key.
back_translation_en: J4.0, The family's trip abroad, "One family, one phone". Before the trip, the caregiver who holds the family's only shared phone requests from Country B's national portal the records of each family member, choosing for each a passcode that the family can say aloud and an expiry date (for example 14 days); the portal records this choice as the holder's consent to sharing (FHIR Consent, IHE Privacy Consent on FHIR). The portal, VHL sharer (IHE ITI VHL) and issuer (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw), issues one passcode-protected verifiable health link per member: the documents (IPS, DVC) encrypted as JWE (<a0>STT-VHL-007</a0>) behind an ITI-YY5 manifest, the link in SMART Health Links payload format at HCERT key 5 (<a1>STT-VHL-001</a1>, <a2>STT-VHL-002</a2>), signed with Country B's DSC. The shared phone holds the QRs for the caregiver, VHL holder. The records themselves stay hosted in Country B: the QR contains only a pointer and a key.

source_en: J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad
back_translation_en: J4.1 Read a family member's records at the point of care abroad

source_en: J4.1. Abroad, a child of the family needs care. The caregiver, the VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL; Holder in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver), opens her QR on the family phone and tells the passcode. The hospital system, a VHL Receiver (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw), verifies the HCERT against the GDHCN trust list, requests the manifest by ITI-YY5 with an HTTP Message Signature (<a0>STT-VHL-005</a0>, <a1>STT-VHL-006</a1>, <a2>STT-VHL-008</a2>) and decrypts the documents (<a3>STT-VHL-007</a3>). Country B's portal checks the passcode, returns the manifest and logs every request, granted or refused, as an AuditEvent at home (IHE BALP). If the HCERT does not verify, there is no digital verification: the VHL is not followed and the records are treated like paper. As in J3, loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the hospital verifies against its cached copy of the trust list and needs no connection to do so. It refreshes that cache nightly or hourly, where an offline site such as the J3 clinic refreshes about weekly.
